title: Boosting trade-offs
prompt: A gradient-boosted tree model’s training loss falls with each extra tree, but the validation loss starts rising. What trade-off does that show, and how would you choose the number of boosting rounds?
objective: Identify overfitting during boosting and use validation to control model complexity.
expected_scope: Interpret the two loss curves, explain why another tree may hurt and propose a validation-based stopping rule.
hint: Which loss tells you about data that did not fit the model?
reference_explanation: Extra stages can improve the fit to training data while making the model predict worse on unseen data. The rising validation loss is evidence of that trade-off. Track validation loss by stage, then select a stage near its minimum or use early stopping with patience. Learning rate and tree depth also affect how quickly the model grows in complexity.

criteria.description: Interprets falling training loss and rising validation loss as evidence of overfitting.
Connects extra boosting stages to greater fitting capacity and a risk to generalisation.
Selects the stage count with validation loss or describes a sound early stopping approach.

critical_misconceptions: Continuing to add trees solely because the training loss decreases.
